intro: The suffixes and prefixes that add size, affection, contempt or intensity to a word.
p.cafecito.consejo: «Café» ends in a stressed vowel, so it takes «-cito»: «cafecito», not «cafito». You also hear «cafelito».
p.poquito.consejo: It comes from «poco». The c becomes qu to keep the k sound: «poco», «poquito».
p.ahorita.consejo: It is «ahora» with «-ita». Widely used in Latin America, it can mean «right now» or «in a little while».
p.chiquillo.consejo: It comes from «chico» plus «-illo»: the c becomes qu. The ll sounds like y: «chi-KI-yo».
p.portazo.consejo: Here «-azo» means «blow»: «dar un portazo» is to slam the door, usually in anger.
p.cochazo.consejo: Here «-azo» means something big and impressive. It is colloquial: «¡Vaya cochazo!».
p.sillón.consejo: It comes from «silla», but with «-ón» the gender changes: «la silla», «el sillón».
p.comilón.consejo: It comes from «comer». «-ón» can mean «someone who does something a lot», as in «dormilón».
p.grandote.consejo: It comes from «grande». «-ote» adds size and a bit of clumsiness. It is colloquial.
p.casucha.consejo: It comes from «casa». «-ucha» adds contempt. Use it carefully, because it can offend.
p.peliculón.consejo: «Película» is feminine, but «peliculón» is masculine: «un peliculón». It is colloquial.
p.requetebién.consejo: «Requete-» is a colloquial prefix that intensifies and is written attached: «requetebién», «requetebueno».
p.archiconocido.consejo: «Archi-» is a prefix that intensifies and is written attached: «archiconocido». It is a bit more formal than «super-».
p.cariñoso.consejo: It comes from «cariño». «-oso» means «full of»: «una abuela cariñosa». The ñ sounds like «ny».
b1.texto:
**Diminutives.** The main one is **-ito / -ita**: casa → **casita**; libro → **librito**; poco → **poquito**. Words ending in **-e**, **-n** or **-r**, and short words, take **-cito** or **-ecito**: café → **cafecito**; joven → **jovencito**; pueblo → **pueblecito**; flor → **florecita**.

Spelling follows the sound: po**c**o → po**qu**ito; ami**g**o → ami**gu**ito.

A diminutive rarely means only «small». It adds affection (**abuelita**), softens a request (**¿Me esperas un momentito?**), or makes something sound unimportant (**un problemilla**). Other endings: **-illo** (chico → **chiquillo**) and **-ín** (pequeño → **pequeñín**). Names take them too, and so do adverbs: **Carlitos**, **Anita**; **ahorita**, **despacito**, **tempranito**.

**Augmentatives.**

- **-ón / -ona**: big, or doing something a lot. **Un sillón** was once a big silla. **Un comilón** eats a lot; **un dormilón** sleeps a lot.
- **-azo**: big and impressive (**un cochazo**, **un golazo**), or a blow given with something (**un portazo**, **un golpazo**, **un codazo**).
- **-ote**: big and a bit clumsy (**grandote**, **un librote**).

Careful: **-ón** changes the gender of some words: **la** silla, **el** sillón; **la** película, **el** peliculón.

**Contempt.** **-ucho** and **-ucha**: **una casucha**, **feúcho**, **un cuartucho**.

**Intensifying prefixes.** Colloquial: **super-** (superbién, superguapo) and **requete-** (requetebién). More formal: **archi-** (archiconocido) and **ultra-**.

**Words that are no longer diminutives.** Some have become independent: **la mesilla** (bedside table), **el bolsillo** (pocket), **la ventanilla** (window of a ticket office), **el cigarrillo**, **el pañuelo**.
b2.f1.texto: Shall I make you a little coffee?
b2.f2.texto: I only want a little bit of coffee, because I am in a hurry.
b2.f3.texto: Wait just a moment, I have kept some doughnuts for you.
b2.f5.texto: Have you seen the neighbour's flashy car?
b2.f6.texto: Last night he slammed the door so hard it woke the whole neighbourhood.
b2.f7.texto: He lives in a hovel and shows off his flashy car.
b4.texto:
Choose the ending according to what you want to say, not only the size.

- **Affection or courtesy**: **-ito, -ita, -cito**. A grandmother says **un cafecito**; a waiter, **un momentito**.
- **Big size**: **-ón, -ona, -ote**. **Un sillón**, **un librote**.
- **Blow or admiration**: **-azo**. **Un portazo** is a blow; **un cochazo** is an impressive car.
- **Contempt**: **-ucho, -ucha, -aco**. **Una casucha**. It can offend, so use it only with people you trust.
- **Intensity**: **super-, requete-, archi-**. **Requetebién** is colloquial; **archiconocido** is a little more formal.

Watch the **gender**: **-ón** can turn a feminine word masculine (la película → el peliculón). And not every diminutive keeps its meaning: **la mesilla** is already a piece of furniture.
b4.e0.texto: This little coffee smells really good.
b4.e1.texto: The big eater sat down in a huge armchair.
b4.e2.texto: My affectionate grandmother keeps me a little bit of cake.
b5.f0.texto: My grandmother's little house always smells of hot coffee.
b5.f1.texto: A huge armchair takes up the corner by the window.
b5.f2.texto: On the table rests a plate of golden doughnuts.
b5.f3.texto: Through the window comes a soft mid-afternoon light.
b5.f4.texto: My grandmother serves the coffee with affectionate hands.
b5.f5.texto: In the street, a big kid hits a ball against the wall.
b5.f6.texto: Every thump echoes between the low houses.
b5.f7.texto: A neighbour sticks her head out and looks on with an angry face.
b5.f8.texto: The slam of her window frightens the sparrows on the roof.
b5.f9.texto: Afterwards the neighbourhood recovers its usual calm.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done: the c becomes qu to keep the k sound.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That does not keep the sound: c before i sounds like th.
b6.o2.refuerzo: A «pocillo» is a small cup, not the diminutive of «poco».
b7.o0.refuerzo: Size does not matter here: «-azo» is something else.
b7.o1: un golpe dado con la puerta
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it: «-azo» can mean a blow.
b8.o0.refuerzo: With «-ón» the word becomes masculine: it is not «peliculona».
b8.o2.refuerzo: That would be a small or unimportant film.
b10.frase: Espera un momentito que ahora vuelvo
b10.traduccion: Wait just a moment, I will be right back
b11.o0: Porque el momento es muy corto
b11.o0.refuerzo: It is not about time, but about politeness.
b11.o1.refuerzo: It is very natural and correct Spanish.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That is it: the diminutive makes asking sound less of a bother.
p.enfado.consejo: From the verb «enfadar», to make someone angry. The word «enfado» is the noun, the feeling itself.
p.asusta.consejo: From «susto», a fright. The s sounds clearly: «a-SUS-ta».
p.recobra.consejo: From «cobrar» with «re-» meaning again. Think of «recovering» your calm.
p.suaviza.consejo: From «suave», soft. The «z» is pronounced like an English «th» in Spain.
p.petición.consejo: From «pedir». The ending «-ción» turns the verb into a noun, so «pedir» becomes «petición».
p.rosquillas.consejo: A small ring-shaped cake, often fried. The «ll» sounds like «y» in most of Spain.
p.despertó.consejo: From «despertar», to wake up. The accent on the «ó» marks the past tense for «él».
p.presume.consejo: From «presumir», to show off. The «m» and «s» are clear, and the stress falls on «SU».
p.casita.consejo: From «casa» with the ending «-ita», which makes it small and cosy. It is very common in Spanish.
p.cariñosas.consejo: From «cariño», affection. The «ñ» sounds «ny», and the feminine plural agrees with «manos».
p.golpazo.consejo: A big «golpe» with the ending «-azo», which makes it stronger. The «z» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.retumba.consejo: A loud sound that repeats through a space. The «r» at the start is strong, and the stress is on «TUM».
